newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London stocks close at record but trade thin.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London stocks close at record but trade thin.

text.p: London stocks hit a closing peak for the second session running on Monday but trade was slow ahead of the Christmas break and other European bourses made only modest gains.
On the currency front, the dollar drifted slightly higher against the mark although business was slack with most dealing rooms winding down for the holiday.

London, Europe's biggest stock exchange, recovered its early losses to close at a record high of 4087.2 points on the FTSE index, drawing strength from Wall Street, which rebounded after an unsteady start.

The climb, a modest 0.24 percent with many trading rooms half empty, was enough to eclipse the peak of 4,077.6 points set only last Friday, when most European bourses were swept higher in a Christmas buying spree on Wall Street.
"We saw a bit of business this morning, some year-end book squaring...but there's no great trend. The market is dying a slow death," said one broker.

The market shrugged off anxieties over minutes of a recent high-level monetary meeting which revealed that Band of England governor Eddie George believed the last interest rate hike was insufficient to meet the government's inflation goal.
British retail shares bounced as traders said they discounted press reports of weak December sales. "In the end, we believe sales will prove to be quite strong," said one market maker.
In Frankfurt, the DAX index, which had surged 1.66 percent on Friday, closed down 0.3 percent after slow business with many traders having already left for the Christmas holidays.
In Paris, shares slipped in and out of profit but registered a gain of 8.91 points to close at 2287.44.
Moulinex was down 3.69 percent at 117.50 at one point. The company on Friday announced it had cut its first half loss and announced plans for a 500 million franc ($95 million) capital increase.
On currency markets, strengthened a little against the mark after a solid rise in U.S. consumer spending in November.
Commerce Department figures said personal incomes rebounded strongly, with big gains in wages and salaries after a flat October, and spending increased 0.5 percent.
Although the most likely scenario was for the dollar to remain at current levels in narrow ranges, any sharp moves on U.S. asset markets would have a knock-on effect, dealers said.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5555 marks and 114.12 yen in late European trade, compared with 1.5521 marks and 114.20 yen on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 9.6 points higher at 4,087.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 8.91 at 2,287.44.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 8.88 at 2,845.57.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $368.85 an ounce, compared to $369.35 on Friday. Silver was unchanged at $4.84.
